label: GCP Overview
desc: Foundational Google Cloud concepts, global footprint, and pricing basics every cloud practitioner should know before diving into individual services.

subs.label: Google Cloud Global Infrastructure
subs.desc: Regions, zones, and Google's private global network backbone that connects them for low-latency, high-throughput data transfer.

subs.label: Google Cloud Platform Overview
subs.desc: High-level overview of Google Cloud's service catalog spanning compute, storage, data analytics, and AI/ML.

subs.label: Google Cloud Pricing
subs.desc: Pay-as-you-go pricing with sustained-use and committed-use discounts, plus the Google Cloud Pricing Calculator for cost estimation.

label: GCP Compute Services
desc: Services for running application code and containers — from fully managed serverless platforms to full control over virtual machines.

subs.label: Cloud Run
subs.desc: Fully managed serverless platform for running stateless containers, automatically scaling to zero when idle.

subs.label: Google App Engine
subs.desc: Fully managed PaaS for building and deploying web applications and APIs without managing the underlying infrastructure.

subs.label: Google Cloud Functions
subs.desc: Event-driven, serverless compute for running single-purpose functions in response to cloud events.

subs.label: Google Compute Engine (GCE)
subs.desc: Customizable, scalable IaaS virtual machines with per-second billing and custom machine types.

subs.label: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)
subs.desc: Managed, production-ready Kubernetes environment with Autopilot mode for hands-off node management.

label: GCP Storage Services
desc: Object, block, and file storage services covering every durability, access-pattern, and cost tier.

subs.label: Google Cloud Filestore
subs.desc: Fully managed NFS file storage for applications that require a shared, POSIX-compliant file system.

subs.label: Google Cloud Storage (GCS)
subs.desc: Unified object storage with Standard, Nearline, Coldline, and Archive classes trading access frequency for cost.

subs.label: Local SSD
subs.desc: High-performance, physically attached SSD storage for VM instances, offering the lowest latency but no data persistence beyond the VM's life.

subs.label: Persistent Disks
subs.desc: Durable, network-attached block storage for VM instances, available in Standard, Balanced, SSD, and Extreme performance tiers.

label: GCP Database Services
desc: Purpose-built managed database engines spanning relational, wide-column, and globally distributed workloads.

subs.label: Google BigQuery
subs.desc: Serverless, highly scalable data warehouse for running fast SQL analytics over petabyte-scale datasets.

subs.label: Google Cloud Bigtable
subs.desc: Fully managed, wide-column NoSQL database built for low-latency, high-throughput workloads like time series and IoT data.

subs.label: Google Cloud SQL
subs.desc: Fully managed relational database service supporting MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server with automated backups and replication.

subs.label: Google Cloud Spanner
subs.desc: Globally distributed, horizontally scalable relational database offering strong consistency and SQL with virtually unlimited scale.

label: GCP Networking & Content Delivery
desc: Services for connecting, routing, and delivering content across virtual networks, on-premises networks, and the public internet.

subs.label: Google Cloud CDN
subs.desc: Content delivery network that caches content at Google's globally distributed edge points of presence.

subs.label: Google Cloud DNS
subs.desc: Scalable, reliable, and managed authoritative DNS service running on the same infrastructure as Google's own DNS.

subs.label: Google Cloud Hybrid Connectivity
subs.desc: Cloud VPN and Cloud Interconnect options for securely connecting on-premises networks to Google Cloud VPCs.

subs.label: Google Cloud Router
subs.desc: Dynamically exchanges routes between a VPC network and on-premises networks using BGP over VPN or Interconnect.

subs.label: Google Cloud Load Balancing
subs.desc: Fully distributed, software-defined load balancing across global and regional layers for HTTP(S), TCP/UDP, and internal traffic.

subs.label: Google Virtual Private Cloud
subs.desc: Global, software-defined network providing isolated, customizable networking with subnets that can span multiple regions.

label: GCP Security and Identity Services
desc: Identity, threat protection, and encryption key management services for securing projects and data.

subs.label: Google Cloud Armor
subs.desc: Web application firewall and DDoS protection service that filters traffic at the edge of Google's network.

subs.label: Google Cloud Identity
subs.desc: Identity-as-a-service platform for managing users, devices, and apps independent of, or alongside, Google Workspace.

subs.label: Google Cloud IAM
subs.desc: Fine-grained access control assigning roles and permissions to members across projects, folders, and organizations.

subs.label: Google Cloud Key Management
subs.desc: Centralized service for creating, managing, and rotating cryptographic keys used to encrypt data across Google Cloud.

subs.label: Google Cloud Secret Manager
subs.desc: Securely stores, manages, and audits access to API keys, passwords, certificates, and other sensitive configuration data.

label: GCP Data and Analytics
desc: Services for querying, processing, and streaming data at scale — the core of Google Cloud's data engineering toolkit.

subs.label: Google Cloud Dataflow
subs.desc: Fully managed service for executing Apache Beam batch and streaming data processing pipelines with autoscaling.

subs.label: Google Cloud Dataprep
subs.desc: Serverless, visual data preparation service (built on Trifacta) for cleaning and transforming raw data for analysis.

subs.label: Google Cloud Dataproc
subs.desc: Fully managed Spark and Hadoop service for running big data processing, ML, and analytics workloads with per-second billing.

subs.label: Google Cloud Pub/Sub
subs.desc: Globally scalable, asynchronous messaging service for building event-driven systems and streaming analytics pipelines.

label: GCP Management Tools
desc: Tools for provisioning infrastructure as code, monitoring, billing, and operating Google Cloud environments.

subs.label: Google Cloud Billing
subs.desc: Tools for tracking, budgeting, and analyzing Google Cloud spend, including budgets, alerts, and detailed cost reports.

subs.label: Google Cloud Console
subs.desc: Web-based graphical interface for managing, monitoring, and configuring all Google Cloud resources and services.

subs.label: Google Cloud Deployment Manager
subs.desc: Infrastructure-as-code service for creating and managing Google Cloud resources using declarative YAML or Python/Jinja templates.

subs.label: Google Cloud Logging
subs.desc: Centralized, real-time log management and analysis service that ingests logs from Google Cloud, on-prem, and other clouds.

subs.label: Google Cloud Monitoring
subs.desc: Collects metrics, uptime checks, and dashboards to provide visibility into the performance and health of applications and infrastructure.

label: GCP Developer Tools
desc: Services for building, testing, and deploying application code and CI/CD pipelines on Google Cloud.

subs.label: Google Cloud Build
subs.desc: Fully managed CI/CD platform that builds, tests, and deploys code across multiple environments and languages.

subs.label: Google Cloud Source Repositories
subs.desc: Fully featured, private Git repositories hosted on Google Cloud with integrated code search and Cloud Build triggers.

subs.label: Google Container Registry
subs.desc: Private Docker image storage (being succeeded by Artifact Registry) integrated with Cloud Build and GKE deployments.

label: Comparison of Google Cloud Services
desc: Head-to-head breakdowns of similar GCP services — the decisions that come up most often in interviews and architecture reviews.

subs.label: Google BigQuery vs BigTable
subs.desc: BigQuery is a SQL-based analytical data warehouse for OLAP queries; Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL store for high-throughput, low-latency operational workloads.

subs.label: GCS vs Persistent Disks vs Local SSD vs Filestore
subs.desc: GCS is global object storage; Persistent Disks are durable VM-attached block storage; Local SSD is ephemeral, ultra-fast VM storage; Filestore is a shared NFS file system.

subs.label: Cloud Functions vs App Engine vs Cloud Run vs GKE
subs.desc: Ordered roughly by control vs simplicity — Cloud Functions for single-purpose events, App Engine for managed apps, Cloud Run for containers with serverless scaling, GKE for full Kubernetes control.

subs.label: Google Compute Engine vs App Engine
subs.desc: Compute Engine gives full VM-level control over the OS and runtime; App Engine abstracts infrastructure entirely so you deploy just code.
